title: JEE Main 2026 · 28 Jan · Shift 2 (recreated)

qs.stem:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The function f : R → R defined by f(x) = x/(1+|x|) is one-one.
Statement II: The function f : R → R defined by f(x) = (x2 + 4x − 30)/(x2 − 8x + 18) is many-one.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: Statement I: for x ≥ 0, f(x) = x/(1+x) is strictly increasing from 0 towards 1; for x < 0, f(x) = x/(1−x) is strictly increasing from −1 up to 0. So f is strictly increasing on R, hence one-one. True.
Statement II: f(0) = −30/18 = −5/3. Solving f(x) = −5/3 gives 3(x<sup>2</sup> + 4x − 30) = −5(x<sup>2</sup> − 8x + 18), i.e. 8x<sup>2</sup> − 28x = 0, so x = 0 or x = 7/2.
Two different inputs give the same value, so f is many-one. True. Both statements are true.
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

qs.stem: Let A be the focus of the parabola y<sup>2</sup> = 8x. Let the line y = mx + c intersect the parabola at two distinct points B and C. If the centroid of the triangle ABC is (7/3, 4/3), then (BC)<sup>2</sup> is equal to:
steps: Here a = 2, so A = (2, 0). Take B = (2t<sub>1</sub><sup>2</sup>, 4t<sub>1</sub>) and C = (2t<sub>2</sub><sup>2</sup>, 4t<sub>2</sub>).

Centroid: (2t<sub>1</sub><sup>2</sup> + 2t<sub>2</sub><sup>2</sup> + 2)/3 = 7/3 gives t<sub>1</sub><sup>2</sup> + t<sub>2</sub><sup>2</sup> = 5/2; (4t<sub>1</sub> + 4t<sub>2</sub>)/3 = 4/3 gives t<sub>1</sub> + t<sub>2</sub> = 1. Then t<sub>1</sub>t<sub>2</sub> = (1 − 5/2)/2 = −3/4 and (t<sub>1</sub> − t<sub>2</sub>)<sup>2</sup> = 1 + 3 = 4.

BC<sup>2</sup> = 4(t<sub>1</sub><sup>2</sup> − t<sub>2</sub><sup>2</sup>)<sup>2</sup> + 16(t<sub>1</sub> − t<sub>2</sub>)<sup>2</sup> = 4(t<sub>1</sub> − t<sub>2</sub>)<sup>2</sup>[(t<sub>1</sub> + t<sub>2</sub>)<sup>2</sup> + 4] = 4 × 4 × 5 = 80.

qs.stem: Let A = {z ∈ C : |z − 2| ≤ 4} and B = {z ∈ C : |z − 2| + |z + 2| = 5}. Then max {|z<sub>1</sub> − z<sub>2</sub>| : z<sub>1</sub> ∈ A and z<sub>2</sub> ∈ B} is:
steps: A is the closed disc with centre (2, 0) and radius 4. B is the ellipse with foci (±2, 0) and major axis 5, so a = 5/2, c = 2, centre at the origin.
For a fixed z<sub>2</sub> on B, the farthest point of the disc is at distance |z<sub>2</sub> − 2| + 4. So we need the largest distance from the centre (2, 0) of the disc to a point of the ellipse.
The farthest point of the ellipse from the focus (2, 0) is the far vertex (−5/2, 0), at distance a + c = 5/2 + 2 = 9/2.

qs.stem:
The probability distribution of a random variable X is given below:
x4k(30/7)k(32/7)k(34/7)k(36/7)k(38/7)k(40/7)k6k
P(x)2/151/152/151/51/152/151/51/15
If E(X) = 263/15, then P(X < 20) is equal to:
steps: E(X) = (k/7)[28·2 + 30·1 + 32·2 + 34·3 + 36·1 + 38·2 + 40·3 + 42·1]/15 = (k/7)(526)/15.
Setting this equal to 263/15 gives 526k/7 = 263, so k = 7/2.
The values become 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, with 20 having probability 1/5 and 21 having probability 1/15.

qs.stem: Let [·] denote the greatest integer function. Then ∫<sub>−π/2</sub><sup>π/2</sup> (12(3 + [x]))/(3 + [sin x] + [cos x]) dx is equal to:
steps: Split at x = −1, 0, 1 (sin 1 ≈ 0.84, cos 1 ≈ 0.54). On [−π/2, −1): [x] = −2, [sin x] = −1, [cos x] = 0, integrand = 12/2 = 6. On [−1, 0): [x] = −1, [sin x] = −1, [cos x] = 0, integrand = 24/2 = 12.
On [0, 1): [x] = 0, [sin x] = 0, [cos x] = 0 (except the single point x = 0), integrand = 36/3 = 12. On [1, π/2): [x] = 1, [sin x] = 0, [cos x] = 0, integrand = 48/3 = 16.

qs.stem: Let the arithmetic mean of 1/a and 1/b be 5/16, a > 2. If α is such that a, 4, α, b are in A.P., then the equation αx<sup>2</sup> − ax + 2(α − 2b) = 0 has:
steps: Let the common difference be d: a = 4 − d, α = 4 + d, b = 4 + 2d. The mean condition gives 1/a + 1/b = 5/8, i.e. (8 + d)/[(4 − d)(4 + 2d)] = 5/8, which simplifies to 5d<sup>2</sup> − 6d − 8 = 0, so d = 2 or d = −4/5.
a > 2 requires d < 2, so d = −4/5: a = 24/5, α = 16/5, b = 12/5.
The equation becomes (16/5)x<sup>2</sup> − (24/5)x + 2(16/5 − 24/5) = 0, i.e. 2x<sup>2</sup> − 3x − 2 = 0, so (2x + 1)(x − 2) = 0 and x = 2, −1/2.
One root (2) lies in (1, 4) and the other (−1/2) in (−2, 0).
opts: one root in (0, 2) and another in (−4, −2)
complex roots of magnitude less than 2
one root in (1, 4) and another in (−2, 0)

qs.stem: Considering the principal values of inverse trigonometric functions, the value of the expression tan(2 sin<sup>−1</sup>(2/√13) − 2 cos<sup>−1</sup>(3/√10)) is equal to:
steps: sin<sup>−1</sup>(2/√13) = tan<sup>−1</sup>(2/3) (opposite 2, adjacent 3) and cos<sup>−1</sup>(3/√10) = tan<sup>−1</sup>(1/3). The expression is tan(2[tan<sup>−1</sup>(2/3) − tan<sup>−1</sup>(1/3)]).
tan<sup>−1</sup>(2/3) − tan<sup>−1</sup>(1/3) = tan<sup>−1</sup>[(1/3)/(1 + 2/9)] = tan<sup>−1</sup>(3/11).

qs.stem: The sum of the coefficients of x<sup>499</sup> and x<sup>500</sup> in (1+x)<sup>1000</sup> + x(1+x)<sup>999</sup> + x<sup>2</sup>(1+x)<sup>998</sup> + … + x<sup>1000</sup> is:
steps: The series is a G.P. with first term (1+x)<sup>1000</sup>, ratio x/(1+x) and 1001 terms. Its sum is (1+x)<sup>1000</sup>[1 − (x/(1+x))<sup>1001</sup>]/[1/(1+x)] = (1+x)<sup>1001</sup> − x<sup>1001</sup>.
The coefficients of x<sup>499</sup> and x<sup>500</sup> are <sup>1001</sup>C<sub>499</sub> and <sup>1001</sup>C<sub>500</sub>.
By Pascal's rule their sum is <sup>1002</sup>C<sub>500</sub>.

qs.stem: The sum of all the elements in the range of f(x) = Sgn(sin x) + Sgn(cos x) + Sgn(tan x) + Sgn(cot x), x ≠ nπ/2, n ∈ Z, where Sgn(t) = 1 if t > 0 and Sgn(t) = −1 if t < 0, is:
steps: Check the sign of (sin, cos, tan, cot) in each quadrant. Quadrant I: (+, +, +, +), f = 4. Quadrant II: (+, −, −, −), f = −2.
Quadrant III: (−, −, +, +), f = 0. Quadrant IV: (−, +, −, −), f = −2.
Range = {−2, 0, 4}, sum = 2.

qs.stem: 6/3<sup>26</sup> + (10·1)/3<sup>25</sup> + (10·2)/3<sup>24</sup> + (10·2<sup>2</sup>)/3<sup>23</sup> + … + (10·2<sup>24</sup>)/3 is equal to:
steps: The terms after the first are 10·2<sup>k</sup>/3<sup>25−k</sup> for k = 0, 1, …, 24, which equal (10/3<sup>25</sup>)·6<sup>k</sup>.
Their sum is (10/3<sup>25</sup>)(6<sup>25</sup> − 1)/5 = 2·6<sup>25</sup>/3<sup>25</sup> − 2/3<sup>25</sup> = 2<sup>26</sup> − 2/3<sup>25</sup>.
Adding the first term 6/3<sup>26</sup> = 2/3<sup>25</sup> cancels the leftover, so the total is 2<sup>26</sup>.

qs.stem: Let Q(a, b, c) be the image of the point P(3, 2, 1) in the line (x − 1)/1 = y/2 = (z − 1)/1. Then the distance of Q from the line (x − 9)/3 = (y − 9)/2 = (z − 5)/(−2) is:
steps: A general point of the first line is N(λ + 1, 2λ, λ + 1). PN = (λ − 2, 2λ − 2, λ) must be perpendicular to (1, 2, 1): (λ − 2) + 2(2λ − 2) + λ = 6λ − 6 = 0, so λ = 1 and N = (2, 2, 2).
N is the midpoint of PQ, so Q = (1, 2, 3).
For the second line take A(9, 9, 5) and d = (3, 2, −2). QA = (8, 7, 2) and QA × d = (−18, 22, −5), with squared magnitude 324 + 484 + 25 = 833; |d|<sup>2</sup> = 17.
Distance = √(833/17) = √49 = 7.

qs.stem: An ellipse has its center at (1, −2), one focus at (3, −2) and one vertex at (5, −2). Then the length of its latus rectum is:
steps: Centre to vertex: a = 5 − 1 = 4. Centre to focus: ae = c = 3 − 1 = 2, so e = 1/2.
b<sup>2</sup> = a<sup>2</sup> − c<sup>2</sup> = 16 − 4 = 12.
Latus rectum = 2b<sup>2</sup>/a = 24/4 = 6.

qs.stem: Let f(x) = ∫ dx/(x<sup>2/3</sup> + 2x<sup>1/2</sup>) be such that f(0) = −26 + 24 log<sub>e</sub>(2). If f(1) = a + b log<sub>e</sub>(3), where a, b ∈ Z, then a + b is equal to:
steps: Put x = t<sup>6</sup>, dx = 6t<sup>5</sup> dt: the integrand becomes 6t<sup>5</sup>/(t<sup>4</sup> + 2t<sup>3</sup>) = 6t<sup>2</sup>/(t + 2) = 6(t − 2) + 24/(t + 2).
So f = 3t<sup>2</sup> − 12t + 24 ln(t + 2) + C with t = x<sup>1/6</sup>.
f(0) = 24 ln 2 + C = −26 + 24 ln 2 gives C = −26.
f(1) (t = 1) = 3 − 12 + 24 ln 3 − 26 = −35 + 24 ln 3, so a = −35, b = 24 and a + b = −11.

qs.stem: Let the circle x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> = 4 intersect x-axis at the points A(a, 0), a > 0 and B(b, 0). Let P(2 cos α, 2 sin α), 0 < α < π/2 and Q(2 cos β, 2 sin β) be two points such that (α − β) = π/2. Then the point of intersection of AQ and BP lies:
steps: A = (2, 0), B = (−2, 0). Let the intersection be (h, k). Slope of BP = sin α/(1 + cos α) = tan(α/2), so k/(h + 2) = tan(α/2) = u. Slope of AQ = sin β/(cos β − 1) = −cot(β/2), so tan(β/2) = v = (2 − h)/k.
From α − β = π/2, tan(α/2 − β/2) = tan(π/4) = 1, so (u − v)/(1 + uv) = 1.
u − v = k/(h + 2) + (h − 2)/k = (k<sup>2</sup> + h<sup>2</sup> − 4)/[k(h + 2)] and 1 + uv = 1 + (2 − h)/(h + 2) = 4/(h + 2).
The ratio is (h<sup>2</sup> + k<sup>2</sup> − 4)/(4k) = 1, so h<sup>2</sup> + k<sup>2</sup> − 4k − 4 = 0: the point lies on x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> − 4y − 4 = 0.

qs.stem:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: 2513 + 2013 + 813 + 313 is divisible by 7.
Statement II: The integral part of (7 + 4√3)25 is an odd number.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: Statement I: for odd n, a + b divides a<sup>n</sup> + b<sup>n</sup>. So 25 + 3 = 28 divides 25<sup>13</sup> + 3<sup>13</sup>, and 20 + 8 = 28 divides 20<sup>13</sup> + 8<sup>13</sup>. Both are multiples of 7, so the sum is divisible by 7. True.

Statement II: let I + f = (7 + 4√3)<sup>25</sup> and f' = (7 − 4√3)<sup>25</sup>, where 0 < f' < 1 (7 − 4√3 ≈ 0.07). The sum (7 + 4√3)<sup>25</sup> + (7 − 4√3)<sup>25</sup> = 2[<sup>25</sup>C<sub>0</sub>7<sup>25</sup> + <sup>25</sup>C<sub>2</sub>7<sup>23</sup>(48) + …] is an even integer.
So I + f + f' is even with 0 < f + f' < 2, hence f + f' = 1 and I is even − 1, an odd number. True. Both statements are true.
opts: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

qs.stem: Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation x dy/dx − y = x<sup>2</sup> cot x, x ∈ (0, π). If y(π/2) = π/2 then 6y(π/6) − 8y(π/4) is equal to:
steps: Divide by x<sup>2</sup>: d/dx(y/x) = (x y' − y)/x<sup>2</sup> = cot x, so y/x = ln sin x + C.
y(π/2) = π/2 gives 1 = ln 1 + C, so C = 1 and y = x ln sin x + x.
y(π/6) = (π/6)(1 − ln 2), so 6y(π/6) = π(1 − ln 2). y(π/4) = (π/4)(1 − (ln 2)/2), so 8y(π/4) = 2π − π ln 2.
Difference = π − π ln 2 − 2π + π ln 2 = −π.

qs.stem: Let P<sub>1</sub> : y = 4x<sup>2</sup> and P<sub>2</sub> : y = x<sup>2</sup> + 27 be two parabolas. If the area of the bounded region enclosed between P<sub>1</sub> and P<sub>2</sub> is six times the area of the bounded region enclosed between the line y = αx, α > 0 and P<sub>1</sub>, then α is equal to:
steps: Intersection: 4x<sup>2</sup> = x<sup>2</sup> + 27 gives x = ±3. Area between P<sub>1</sub> and P<sub>2</sub> = ∫<sub>−3</sub><sup>3</sup>(27 − 3x<sup>2</sup>)dx = 2[27x − x<sup>3</sup>]<sub>0</sub><sup>3</sup> = 2(81 − 27) = 108.
Line y = αx meets y = 4x<sup>2</sup> at x = α/4. Area = ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>α/4</sup>(αx − 4x<sup>2</sup>)dx = α<sup>3</sup>/32 − α<sup>3</sup>/48 = α<sup>3</sup>/96.
108 = 6α<sup>3</sup>/96 gives α<sup>3</sup> = 1728, so α = 12.

qs.stem: Let the ellipse E : x<sup>2</sup>/144 + y<sup>2</sup>/169 = 1 and the hyperbola H : x<sup>2</sup>/16 − y<sup>2</sup>/λ<sup>2</sup> = −1 have the same foci. If e and L respectively denote the eccentricity and the length of the latus rectum of H, then the value of 24(e + L) is:
steps: For E the major axis is along y (169 > 144): c<sup>2</sup> = 169 − 144 = 25, so the foci are (0, ±5).
H is y<sup>2</sup>/λ<sup>2</sup> − x<sup>2</sup>/16 = 1 with foci at distance √(λ<sup>2</sup> + 16) = 5, so λ = 3. Then e = 5/3.

qs.stem: If the distance of the point P(43, α, β), β < 0, from the line r = 4i − k + μ(2i + 3k), μ ∈ R along a line with direction ratios 3, −1, 0 is 13√10 then α2 + β2 is equal to ________.
steps: Moving from P along (3, −1, 0) by parameter λ gives (43 + 3λ, α − λ, β). It reaches the line (points (4 + 2μ, 0, −1 + 3μ)) when α − λ = 0, so λ = α.
The distance is |λ|√(9 + 1) = |α|√10 = 13√10, so |α| = 13.
Matching coordinates: 4 + 2μ = 43 + 3α and β = 3μ − 1 give β = (115 + 9α)/2. For α = 13, β = 116 > 0 (rejected); for α = −13, β = −1 < 0.
α<sup>2</sup> + β<sup>2</sup> = 169 + 1 = 170.

qs.stem: Let f be a differentiable function satisfying f(x) = 1 − 2x + ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>x</sup> e<sup>(x−t)</sup> f(t) dt, x ∈ R and let g(x) = ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>x</sup> (f(t) + 2)<sup>15</sup> (t − 4)<sup>6</sup> (t + 12)<sup>17</sup> dt, x ∈ R. If p and q are respectively the points of local minima and local maxima of g, then the value of |p + q| is equal to ________.
steps: Write f(x) = 1 − 2x + e<sup>x</sup>∫<sub>0</sub><sup>x</sup> e<sup>−t</sup>f(t)dt and differentiate: f'(x) = −2 + f(x) + [f(x) − 1 + 2x] = 2f + 2x − 3, with f(0) = 1. The function f(x) = 1 − x satisfies this and f(0) = 1, so it is the solution.
g'(x) = (3 − x)<sup>15</sup>(x − 4)<sup>6</sup>(x + 12)<sup>17</sup>. Sign: negative for x < −12, positive on (−12, 3), negative for x > 3 (x = 4 is an even-power root, no sign change).
So x = −12 is a local minimum (p = −12) and x = 3 is a local maximum (q = 3).

qs.stem: If ∑<sub>r=1</sub><sup>25</sup> (r/(r<sup>4</sup> + r<sup>2</sup> + 1)) = p/q, where p and q are positive integers such that gcd(p, q) = 1, then p + q is equal to ________.
steps: r<sup>4</sup> + r<sup>2</sup> + 1 = (r<sup>2</sup> + r + 1)(r<sup>2</sup> − r + 1), and their difference is 2r. So r/(r<sup>4</sup> + r<sup>2</sup> + 1) = (1/2)[1/(r<sup>2</sup> − r + 1) − 1/(r<sup>2</sup> + r + 1)].
Since (r + 1)<sup>2</sup> − (r + 1) + 1 = r<sup>2</sup> + r + 1, the sum telescopes: (1/2)[1/1 − 1/(25<sup>2</sup> + 25 + 1)] = (1/2)(1 − 1/651) = 325/651.
651 = 3×7×31 and 325 = 5<sup>2</sup>×13 share no factor, so p + q = 325 + 651 = 976.

qs.stem: Let A = [[3, −4], [1, −1]] and B be two matrices such that A<sup>100</sup> = 100B + I. Then the sum of all the elements of B<sup>100</sup> is ________.
steps: Write A = I + M with M = [[2, −4], [1, −2]]. Then M<sup>2</sup> = [[4 − 4, −8 + 8], [2 − 2, −4 + 4]] = 0.
Since I and M commute and M<sup>2</sup> = 0, A<sup>100</sup> = (I + M)<sup>100</sup> = I + 100M. Comparing with 100B + I gives B = M.
B<sup>100</sup> = M<sup>100</sup> = 0, so the sum of its elements is 0.

qs.stem: Three persons enter in a lift at the ground floor. The lift will go upto 10<sup>th</sup> floor. The number of ways, in which the three persons can exit the lift at three different floors, if the lift does not stop at first, second and third floors, is equal to ________.
steps: The allowed exit floors are 4 to 10, which is 7 floors.
Choose 3 different floors in <sup>7</sup>C<sub>3</sub> = 35 ways and assign them to the three persons in 3! = 6 ways.
Total = 35 × 6 = 210.

qs.stem:
Identify the correct statements :
A. Electrostatic field lines form closed loops.
B. The electric field lines point radially outward when charge is greater than zero.
C. The Gauss - Law is valid only for inverse - square force.
D. The workdone in moving a charged particle in a static electric field around a closed path is zero.
E. The motion of a particle under Coulomb's force must take place in a plane.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
steps: A is false: electrostatic field lines start on positive and end on negative charge, they never close (the field is conservative).
B (for a positive charge), C (Gauss's law holds because the force goes as 1/r<sup>2</sup>) and D (conservative field, zero work over a closed path) are true.
E is true: Coulomb force is central, so angular momentum is conserved and the path stays in one plane.
True set: B, C, D, E.

qs.stem: The mean free path of a molecule of diameter 5×10<sup>−10</sup> m at the temperature 41°C, and pressure 1.38×10<sup>5</sup> Pa, is given as ________ m. (Given k<sub>B</sub> = 1.38×10<sup>−23</sup> J/K).
steps: λ = k<sub>B</sub>T / (√2 π d<sup>2</sup> P), with T = 41 + 273 = 314 K.
Numerator: 1.38×10<sup>−23</sup> × 314 = 4.33×10<sup>−21</sup>.
Denominator: √2 × π × 25×10<sup>−20</sup> × 1.38×10<sup>5</sup> = 1.53×10<sup>−13</sup>.
λ = 2.83×10<sup>−8</sup> m = 2√2 ×10<sup>−8</sup> m.

qs.stem: The speed of a longitudinal wave in a metallic bar is 400 m/s. If the density and Young's modulus of the bar material are increased by 0.5 % and 1%, respectively then the speed of the wave is changed approximately to ________ m/s.
steps: v = √(Y/ρ), so Δv/v = (1/2)(ΔY/Y − Δρ/ρ).
New speed = 400 × 1.0025 = 401 m/s.

qs.stem:
Match List I with List - II.
List - I: A. Coefficient of viscosity; B. Surface tension; C. Pressure; D. Surface energy
List - II: I. [ML−1T−2]; II. [ML2T−2]; III. [ML0T−2]; IV. [ML−1T−1]
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
steps: Viscosity η = F/(A dv/dx): [ML<sup>−1</sup>T<sup>−1</sup>] gives A-IV.
Surface tension = force/length = [MT<sup>−2</sup>] = [ML<sup>0</sup>T<sup>−2</sup>] gives B-III.
Pressure = force/area = [ML<sup>−1</sup>T<sup>−2</sup>] gives C-I; surface energy = energy = [ML<sup>2</sup>T<sup>−2</sup>] gives D-II.

qs.stem:
Identify the correct statements :
A. Effective capacitance of a series combination of capacitors is always smaller than the smallest capacitance of the capacitor in the combination.
B. When a dielectric medium is placed between the charged plates of a capacitor, displacement of charges cannot occur due to insulation property of dielectric.
C. Increasing of area of capacitor plate or decreasing of thickness of dielectric is an alternate method to increase the capacitance.
D. For a point charge, concentric spherical shells centered at the location of the charge are equipotential surfaces.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
steps: A: 1/C<sub>eq</sub> = ∑1/C<sub>i</sub> exceeds 1/C<sub>min</sub>, so C<sub>eq</sub> is smaller than every C<sub>i</sub>: true.
B is false: a dielectric gets polarised (bound charges are displaced slightly) even though it is an insulator.
C: C = εA/d grows with larger A or smaller d: true. D: potential kq/r is constant on a sphere centred on the charge: true.
Correct: A, C and D.

qs.stem: As shown in the figure, a spring (k = 150 N/m) is kept in a stretched position with some extension by holding the masses 1 kg and 0.2 kg (one at each end of the spring) with a separation more than spring natural length and are released. Assuming the horizontal surface to be frictionless, the angular frequency (in SI unit) of the system is :
steps: Two masses joined by a spring on a smooth surface oscillate with the reduced mass μ = m<sub>1</sub>m<sub>2</sub>/(m<sub>1</sub>+m<sub>2</sub>).
ω = √(k/μ) = √(150 × 6) = √900 = 30 rad/s.

qs.stem: When the position vector r = xi + yj + zk changes sign as −r, which one of the following vector will not flip under sign change ?
steps: Under r → −r, velocity, acceleration and linear momentum (all derived from r by differentiation or multiplication by a scalar) change sign (polar vectors).
Angular momentum L = r × p: both factors flip, so the product is unchanged (axial vector).
Hence angular momentum does not flip.

qs.stem: A small block of mass m slides down from the top of a frictionless inclined surface, while the inclined plane is moving towards left with constant acceleration a<sub>0</sub>. The angle between the inclined plane and ground is θ and its base length is L. Assuming that initially the small block is at the top of the inclined plane, the time it takes to reach the lowest point of the inclined plane is _______ .
steps: Work in the incline's frame: the pseudo-force m a<sub>0</sub> acts to the right (opposite to the incline's leftward acceleration); the block slides down towards the left.
Along the incline (downwards) acceleration a = g sinθ − a<sub>0</sub> cosθ. Incline length s = L/cosθ.
s = (1/2)a t<sup>2</sup> gives t<sup>2</sup> = 2L/(g sinθ cosθ − a<sub>0</sub> cos<sup>2</sup>θ).
Using sinθ cosθ = (sin2θ)/2 and cos<sup>2</sup>θ = (1 + cos2θ)/2: t = √(4L/(g sin2θ − a<sub>0</sub>(1 + cos2θ))).

qs.stem: Two p-n junction diodes D<sub>1</sub> and D<sub>2</sub> are connected as shown in figure. A and B are input signals and C is the output. The given circuit will function as a _______ .
steps: The anodes of D<sub>1</sub> and D<sub>2</sub> join at the output node C, which is pulled up to 5 V through R; the cathodes are the inputs A and B.
If either input is low (0), that diode is forward biased and pulls C to about 0 V.
Only when both A and B are high does neither diode conduct, so C stays high (5 V).
C is high only for A = B = 1: AND gate.

qs.stem: A Wheatstone bridge is initially at room temperature and all arms of the bridge have same value of resistances (R<sub>1</sub> = R<sub>2</sub> = R<sub>3</sub> = R<sub>4</sub>). When R<sub>3</sub> resistance is heated to some temperature, its resistance value has gone up by 10%. The potential difference (V<sub>a</sub> − V<sub>b</sub>) (after R<sub>3</sub> is heated ) is _______ V. (40 V battery; R<sub>1</sub>, R<sub>3</sub> in the upper arms, R<sub>2</sub>, R<sub>4</sub> in the lower arms; V<sub>a</sub> is the left junction, V<sub>b</sub> the right junction.)
steps: Take the bottom node as 0 V and the top as 40 V. Left branch (R<sub>1</sub>, R<sub>2</sub> equal): V<sub>a</sub> = 20 V.
Right branch: V<sub>b</sub> = 40 × R<sub>4</sub>/(R<sub>3</sub> + R<sub>4</sub>) = 40 × R/(1.1R + R) = 40/2.1 = 19.05 V.
V<sub>a</sub> − V<sub>b</sub> = 20 − 19.05 ≈ 0.95 V.

qs.stem: A biconvex lens is formed by using two thin planoconvex lenses, as shown in the figure. The refractive index and radius of curved surfaces are also mentioned in figure (left half: μ = 1.5, curved surface radius 15 cm; right half: μ = 1.2, curved surface radius 12 cm). When an object is placed on the left side of lens at a distance of 30 cm from the biconvex lens, the magnification of the image will be :
steps: Power of each plano-convex half: P = (μ − 1)/R. Left: 0.5/15 = 1/30 cm<sup>−1</sup>; right: 0.2/12 = 1/60 cm<sup>−1</sup>.
Thin lenses in contact: P = 1/30 + 1/60 = 1/20, so f = 20 cm.
Object u = −30 cm: 1/v = 1/20 − 1/30 = 1/60, v = 60 cm.
m = v/u = 60/(−30) = −2.

qs.stem: In an experiment, a set of reading are obtained as follows −1.24 mm, 1.25 mm, 1.23 mm, 1.21 mm, 1.21 mm. The expected least count of the instrument used in recording these readings is ______ mm.
steps: All readings are recorded to the second decimal place (hundredths of a mm).
So the smallest division the instrument resolves is 0.01 mm (e.g. a screw gauge).

qs.stem: Which one of the following is not a measurable quantity ?
steps: Only differences of electric potential can be measured with a voltmeter; the absolute potential at a point depends on an arbitrary zero and cannot be measured.
Voltage difference and resistance are directly measurable, so the non-measurable one is (absolute) voltage.

qs.stem: A plane electromagnetic wave is moving in free space with velocity c = 3×108 m/s and its electric field is given as E = 54 sin(kz − ωt) j V/m, where j is the unit vector along y-axis. The magnetic field vector B of the wave is :
steps: The wave travels along +z. Amplitude B<sub>0</sub> = E<sub>0</sub>/c = 54/(3×10<sup>8</sup>) = 1.8×10<sup>−7</sup> T.
Direction: E × B must point along +z. j × (−i) = +k, so B is along −i.
B = −1.8×10−7 sin(kz − ωt) i T.

qs.stem:
A particle starts moving from time t = 0 and its coordinate is given as x(t) = 4t3 − 3t
A. The particle returns to its original position (origin) 0.866 units later
B. The particle is 1 unit away from origin at its turning point
C. Acceleration of the particle is non-negative
D. The particle is 0.5 units away from origin at its turning point
E. Particle never turns back as acceleration is non-negative
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
steps: x = 0 gives t(4t<sup>2</sup> − 3) = 0, so t = √3/2 = 0.866: A true.
v = 12t<sup>2</sup> − 3 = 0 at t = 0.5; x(0.5) = 0.5 − 1.5 = −1, so the turning point is 1 unit from the origin: B true, D false.
a = 24t ≥ 0 for t ≥ 0: C true. The velocity changes sign at t = 0.5 (it does turn back), so E is false.

qs.stem: Number of photons of equal energy emitted per second by a 6 mW laser source operating at 663 nm is _________. (Given h = 6.63×10<sup>−34</sup> J.s and c = 3×10<sup>8</sup> m/s) :
steps: Energy per photon E = hc/λ = (6.63×10<sup>−34</sup> × 3×10<sup>8</sup>)/(663×10<sup>−9</sup>) = 3×10<sup>−19</sup> J.
Photons per second n = P/E = (6×10<sup>−3</sup>)/(3×10<sup>−19</sup>) = 2×10<sup>16</sup>.

qs.stem: For a transparent prism, if the angle of minimum deviation is equal to its refracting angle, the refractive index n of the prism satisfies.
steps: With δ<sub>min</sub> = A: n = sin((A + δ)/2)/sin(A/2) = sin A / sin(A/2) = 2cos(A/2).
Since A < 180°, cos(A/2) < 1, so n < 2.
At minimum deviation the incidence angle is i = (A + δ)/2 = A and must be below 90°, so A < 90° and cos(A/2) > 1/√2, giving n > √2.
Therefore √2 < n < 2.

qs.stem: A nucleus has mass number α and radius R<sub>α</sub>. Another nucleus has mass number β and radius R<sub>β</sub>. If β = 8α then R<sub>α</sub>/R<sub>β</sub> is :
steps: Nuclear radius R = R<sub>0</sub>A<sup>1/3</sup>.
R<sub>α</sub>/R<sub>β</sub> = (α/β)<sup>1/3</sup> = (1/8)<sup>1/3</sup> = 1/2 = 0.5.

qs.stem:
A long cylindrical conductor with large cross section carries an electric current distributed uniformly over its cross-section. Magnetic field due to this current is :
A. maximum at either ends of the conductor and minimum at the midpoint
B. maximum at the axis of the conductor
C. minimum at the surface of the conductor
D. minimum at the axis of the conductor
E. same at all points in the cross-section of the conductor
steps: Ampere's law inside the conductor (r < R): B = μ<sub>0</sub>Ir/(2πR<sup>2</sup>), growing linearly with r; outside it falls as 1/r.
So B = 0 on the axis (minimum) and is maximum at the surface.
Only D is correct; A concerns the length of a long conductor (no end effects) and is not true, and B, C, E are false.

qs.stem: An inductor stores 16 J of magnetic field energy and dissipates 32 W of thermal energy due to its resistance when an a.c. current of 2 A (rms) and frequency 50 Hz flows through it. The ratio of inductive reactance to its resistance is ________. (π = 3.14)
steps: Power: I<sub>rms</sub><sup>2</sup>R = 32, so R = 32/4 = 8 Ω.
Energy (1/2)LI<sup>2</sup> = 16 with I = 2 A gives L = 8 H.
X<sub>L</sub> = 2πfL = 2 × 3.14 × 50 × 8 = 2512 Ω.

qs.stem: Two tuning forks A and B are sounded together giving rise to 8 beats in 2 s. When fork A is loaded with wax, the beat frequency is reduced to 4 beats in 2 s. If the original frequency of tuning fork B is 380 Hz then original frequency of tuning fork A is _________ Hz.
steps: Beat frequency originally 8/2 = 4 Hz, after loading 4/2 = 2 Hz.
Loading with wax lowers f<sub>A</sub>; the beat frequency fell, so f<sub>A</sub> was above f<sub>B</sub>.
f<sub>A</sub> = 380 + 4 = 384 Hz (after loading 382 Hz, beating 2 Hz).

qs.stem: A thermodynamic system is taken through the cyclic process ABC as shown in the figure (A: V = 2 m<sup>3</sup>, P = 100 Pa; B: V = 5 m<sup>3</sup>, P = 300 Pa; C: V = 5 m<sup>3</sup>, P = 100 Pa; path A→B→C→A). The total work done by the system during the cycle ABC is ________ J.
steps: Work in a cycle equals the area enclosed on the P-V diagram: a right triangle with base (5 − 2) = 3 m<sup>3</sup> and height (300 − 100) = 200 Pa.
Area = (1/2) × 3 × 200 = 300 J.
The path A→B→C→A is clockwise, so the work done by the system is positive: 300 J.

qs.stem: A fly wheel having mass 3 kg and radius 5 m is free to rotate about a horizontal axis. A string having negligible mass is wound around the wheel and the loose end of the string is connected to 3 kg mass. The mass is kept at rest initially and released. Kinetic energy of the wheel when the mass descends by 3 m is ________ J. (g = 10 m/s<sup>2</sup>)
steps: Treat the wheel as a uniform disc, I = (1/2)MR<sup>2</sup>; with no slipping ω = v/R, so wheel KE = (1/4)Mv<sup>2</sup>.
Energy conservation: mgh = (1/2)mv<sup>2</sup> + (1/4)Mv<sup>2</sup> gives 3 × 10 × 3 = 90 = 1.5v<sup>2</sup> + 0.75v<sup>2</sup> = 2.25v<sup>2</sup>, so v<sup>2</sup> = 40.
Wheel KE = (1/4) × 3 × 40 = 30 J.

qs.stem: A beam of light consisting of wavelengths 650 nm and 550 nm illuminates the Young's double slits with separation of 2 mm such that the interference fringes are formed on a screen, placed at a distance of 1.2 m from the slits. The least distance of a point from the central maximum, where the bright fringes due to both the wavelengths coincide, is _________ × 10<sup>−5</sup> m.
steps: Bright fringes coincide when n<sub>1</sub>(650) = n<sub>2</sub>(550), i.e. n<sub>1</sub>/n<sub>2</sub> = 11/13, so the smallest integers are n<sub>1</sub> = 11, n<sub>2</sub> = 13.
y = n<sub>1</sub>λ<sub>1</sub>D/d = 11 × 650×10<sup>−9</sup> × 1.2 / (2×10<sup>−3</sup>).
y = 11 × 3.9×10<sup>−4</sup> = 4.29×10<sup>−3</sup> m = 429 × 10<sup>−5</sup> m.

qs.stem:
Identify the correct statements:
The presence of −NO2 group in benzene ring
A. activates the ring towards electrophilic substitutions.
B. deactivates the ring towards electrophilic substitutions.
C. activates the ring towards nucleophilic substitutions.
D. deactivates the ring towards nucleophilic substitutions.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: −NO<sub>2</sub> withdraws electrons by −M and −I effects, so the ring becomes electron poor.
An electron-poor ring is attacked less readily by electrophiles, so it is deactivated towards electrophilic substitution (B true, A false).

The same electron deficiency stabilises the negatively charged intermediate of nucleophilic substitution (especially with o/p-nitro), so the ring is activated towards nucleophiles (C true, D false). Answer: B and C.

qs.stem: A student has been given 0.314 g of an organic compound and asked to estimate Sulphur. During the experiment, the student has obtained 0.4813 g of barium sulphate. The percentage of sulphur present in the compound is _______ (Given Molar mass in g mol<sup>−1</sup> S : 32, BaSO<sub>4</sub> : 233)
steps: All sulphur ends up in BaSO<sub>4</sub>: mass of S = (32)/(233) × 0.4813 g = 0.0661 g.

qs.stem:
A student performed analysis of aliphatic organic compound 'X' which on analysis gave C = 61.01%, H = 15.25%, N = 23.74%.
This compound, on treatment with HNO2/H2O produced another compound 'Y' which did not contain any nitrogen atom. However, the compound 'Y' upon controlled oxidation produced another compound 'Z' that responded to iodoform test.
The structure of 'X' is:
steps: Mole ratio C : H : N = 61.01/12 : 15.25/1 : 23.74/14 = 5.08 : 15.25 : 1.70 = 3 : 9 : 1, so X is C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>9</sub>N (C = 36/59 = 61%). This rules out the butyl and phenyl amines.
Primary amine + HNO<sub>2</sub> gives the alcohol Y (N-free). Propylamine would give propan-1-ol, then propanal, which fails the iodoform test.
Isopropylamine gives propan-2-ol, which oxidises to acetone (Z), a methyl ketone that gives the iodoform test. So X = (CH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub>CH−NH<sub>2</sub>.

qs.stem:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The increasing order of boiling point of hydrogen halides is HCl < HBr < HI < HF.
Statement II: The increasing order of melting point of hydrogen halides is HCl < HBr < HF < HI.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: Boiling points: HCl (188 K) < HBr (206 K) < HI (238 K) < HF (293 K). van der Waals forces grow with size, and HF is highest because of strong hydrogen bonding. Statement I is true.
Melting points: HCl (159 K) < HBr (186 K) < HF (190 K) < HI (222 K). The crystal packing makes HF's melting point only slightly above HBr, but below HI. Statement II is true.
opts: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

qs.stem:
The correct order of acidic strength of the major products formed in the given reactions, is:
A. PhNH2 → (1) NaNO2 + HCl (< 5°C); (2) CuCN; (3) H3O+/Δ → [A]
B. CH3CH2CHO → [Ag(NH3)2]+, OH−, Δ → [B]
C. CH4 + O2 → (i) Mo2O3; (ii) Na2Cr2O7/H+ → [C]
D. PhCH2MgBr + CO2 → (dry ether), then H3O+ → [D]
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: Products: A = benzoic acid (diazonium, cyanide, hydrolysis); B = propanoic acid (Tollens oxidation); C = formic acid (methane to methanal to acid); D = phenylacetic acid (Grignard + CO<sub>2</sub>).
Acidity: HCOOH (no electron-donating group, K<sub>a</sub> 1.8×10<sup>−4</sup>) > benzoic acid (6.3×10<sup>−5</sup>) > phenylacetic acid (4.9×10<sup>−5</sup>) > propanoic acid (1.3×10<sup>−5</sup>).
So C > A > D > B.

qs.stem:
Consider the following aqueous solutions.
I. 2.2 g Glucose in 125 mL of solution.
II. 1.9 g Calcium chloride in 250 mL of solution.
III. 9.0 g Urea in 500 mL of solution.
IV. 20.5 g Aluminium sulphate in 750 mL of solution.
The correct increasing order of boiling point of these solutions will be:
[Given: Molar mass in g mol−1: H = 1, C = 12, N = 14, O = 16, Cl = 35.5, Ca = 40, Al = 27 and S = 32]
steps: For dilute solutions the boiling point elevation is proportional to i × c (molarity ≈ molality).
Increasing boiling point: I < II < III < IV.

qs.stem:
Consider the following statements about manganate and permanganate ions. Identify the correct statements.
A. The geometry of both manganate and permanganate ions is tetrahedral.
B. The oxidation states of Mn in manganate and permanganate are +7 and +6, respectively.
C. Oxidation of Mn(II) salt by peroxodisulphate gives manganate ion as the final product.
D. Manganate ion is paramagnetic and permanganate ions is diamagnetic.
E. Acidified permanganate ion reduces oxalate, nitrite and iodide ions.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: MnO<sub>4</sub><sup>2−</sup> (Mn +6, d<sup>1</sup>, paramagnetic) and MnO<sub>4</sub><sup>−</sup> (Mn +7, d<sup>0</sup>, diamagnetic) are both tetrahedral: A and D true.
B has the oxidation states reversed, so it is false.

Mn<sup>2+</sup> with S<sub>2</sub>O<sub>8</sub><sup>2−</sup> gives permanganate, not manganate: C false. Permanganate is an oxidant, it oxidises (not reduces) oxalate, nitrite and iodide: E false. Answer: A and D only.

qs.stem:
Total number of alkali insoluble solid sulphonamides obtained by reaction of given amines with Hinsberg's reagent is _____ .
Aniline, N-Methylaniline, Methanamine, N,N-Dimethylmethanamine, N-Methyl methanamine, Phenylmethanamine, N-propylaniline, N-phenylaniline, N,N-Dimethylaniline, Allylamine, Isopropylamine
steps: Hinsberg's reagent (benzenesulphonyl chloride) gives an alkali-insoluble sulphonamide only with secondary amines, because the product has no acidic N−H. Primary amines give alkali-soluble products and tertiary amines do not react.
Secondary amines in the list: N-methylaniline, N-methylmethanamine (dimethylamine), N-propylaniline and N-phenylaniline.
Count = 4.

qs.stem:
Consider the following reactions
Na2B4O7 →(Δ) 2X + Y
CuSO4 + Y →(Non-luminous flame) Z + SO3
2Z + 2X + Carbon →(Luminous flame) 2Q + Na2B4O7 + CO
The oxidation states of Cu in Z and Q, respectively are:
steps: Heating borax gives NaBO<sub>2</sub> (X) and B<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> (Y).
CuSO<sub>4</sub> + B<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> gives Cu(BO<sub>2</sub>)<sub>2</sub> (Z) + SO<sub>3</sub>, so Cu is +2 in Z (blue bead in oxidising flame).

In the reducing (luminous) flame carbon reduces it: 2Cu(BO<sub>2</sub>)<sub>2</sub> + 2NaBO<sub>2</sub> + C gives 2CuBO<sub>2</sub> + Na<sub>2</sub>B<sub>4</sub>O<sub>7</sub> + CO, so Q = CuBO<sub>2</sub> with Cu +1.

qs.stem:
The reactions which produce alcohol as the product are:
A. CH4 + O2 →(Mo2O3, Δ)
B. 2CH3CH3 + 3O2 →((CH3COO)2Mn, Δ)
C. (CH3)3CH →(KMnO4)
D. 2CH4 + O2 →(Cu/523 K/100 atm)
E. CH3−CH=CH−CH3 →(KMnO4/H+)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: A: controlled oxidation over Mo<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> gives methanal (HCHO), not an alcohol.
B: ethane with Mn(OAc)<sub>2</sub> gives ethanoic acid. E: acidic KMnO<sub>4</sub> cleaves but-2-ene to ethanoic acid.
C: KMnO<sub>4</sub> oxidises the tertiary C−H of isobutane to give (CH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>3</sub>C−OH. D: methane with Cu at 523 K/100 atm gives methanol. So C and D.

qs.stem: Consider the elements N, P, O, S, Cl and F. The number of valence electrons present in the elements with most and least metallic character from the above list is respectively.
steps: Metallic character decreases across a period and increases down a group, so the most metallic element here is P (group 15, third period) and the least metallic is F.
P has 5 valence electrons and F has 7.

qs.stem: The correct increasing order of spin-only magnetic moment values of the complex ions [MnBr<sub>4</sub>]<sup>2−</sup> (A), [Cu(H<sub>2</sub>O)<sub>6</sub>]<sup>2+</sup> (B), [Ni(CN)<sub>4</sub>]<sup>2−</sup> (C) and [Ni(H<sub>2</sub>O)<sub>6</sub>]<sup>2+</sup> (D) is:
steps: Unpaired electrons: [MnBr<sub>4</sub>]<sup>2−</sup>: Mn<sup>2+</sup> d<sup>5</sup>, weak-field tetrahedral, n = 5. [Cu(H<sub>2</sub>O)<sub>6</sub>]<sup>2+</sup>: d<sup>9</sup>, n = 1.
[Ni(CN)<sub>4</sub>]<sup>2−</sup>: d<sup>8</sup> square planar, n = 0. [Ni(H<sub>2</sub>O)<sub>6</sub>]<sup>2+</sup>: d<sup>8</sup> octahedral, n = 2.
μ = √(n(n+2)) increases with n: C (0) < B (1) < D (2) < A (5).

qs.stem:
Observe the following equilibrium in a 1 L flask.
A(g) ⇌ B(g)
At T(K), the equilibrium concentrations of A and B are 0.5 M and 0.375 M respectively. 0.1 moles of A is added into the flask and heated to T(K) to establish the equilibrium again. The new equilibrium concentrations (in M) of A and B are respectively
steps: After adding 0.1 mol, [A] = 0.6 M. The reaction shifts forward by x: 0.75 = (0.375 + x)/(0.6 − x).

qs.stem: The wavelength of photon 'A' is 400 nm. The frequency of photon 'B' is 10<sup>16</sup> s<sup>−1</sup>. The wave number of photon 'C' is 10<sup>4</sup> cm<sup>−1</sup>. The correct order of energy of these photons is:
steps: Convert to wavelength. A: 400 nm. B: λ = c/ν = (3×10<sup>8</sup>)/(10<sup>16</sup>) = 3×10<sup>−8</sup> m = 30 nm. C: λ = 1/(10<sup>4</sup> cm<sup>−1</sup>) = 10<sup>−4</sup> cm = 1000 nm.
E = hc/λ is inversely proportional to λ, so B (30 nm) > A (400 nm) > C (1000 nm).

qs.stem:
Match List-I with List-II according to shape.
List-I: A. XeO3; B. XeF2; C. XeO2F2; D. XeOF4
List-II: I. BrF5; II. NH3; III. [I3]−; IV. SF4
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: XeO<sub>3</sub>: sp<sup>3</sup>, 3 bond pairs + 1 lone pair, pyramidal like NH<sub>3</sub> (II).
XeF<sub>2</sub>: sp<sup>3</sup>d with 3 lone pairs, linear like I<sub>3</sub><sup>−</sup> (III).
XeO<sub>2</sub>F<sub>2</sub>: trigonal bipyramidal with 1 lone pair, see-saw like SF<sub>4</sub> (IV).
XeOF<sub>4</sub>: octahedral arrangement with 1 lone pair, square pyramidal like BrF<sub>5</sub> (I).

qs.stem: The plot of log<sub>10</sub> K vs 1/T gives a straight line. The intercept and slope respectively are (where K is equilibrium constant).
steps: From ΔG° = −2.303RT log K = ΔH° − TΔS°, log K = −ΔH°/(2.303R) · (1/T) + ΔS°/(2.303R).
Comparing with y = mx + c: slope = −ΔH°/(2.303R), intercept = ΔS°/(2.303R). Intercept first, then slope: option 2.

qs.stem:
For the given reaction;
CaCO3 + 2HCl → CaCl2 + H2O + CO2
If 90 g CaCO3 is added to 300 mL of HCl which contains 38.55% HCl by mass and has density 1.13 g mL−1, then which of the following option is correct?
Given molar mass of H, Cl, Ca and O are 1, 35.5, 40 and 16 g mol−1 respectively.
steps: CaCO<sub>3</sub> = 90/100 = 0.9 mol, which needs 1.8 mol HCl, so CaCO<sub>3</sub> is limiting and is fully used.

qs.stem: The number of isoelectronic species among Sc<sup>3+</sup>, Cr<sup>2+</sup>, Mn<sup>3+</sup>, Co<sup>3+</sup> and Fe<sup>3+</sup> is 'n'. If 'n' moles of AgCl is formed during the reaction of complex with formula CoCl<sub>3</sub>(en)<sub>2</sub>NH<sub>3</sub> with excess of AgNO<sub>3</sub> solution, then the number of electrons present in the t<sub>2g</sub> orbital of the complex is _______.
steps: Electron counts: Sc<sup>3+</sup> 18, Cr<sup>2+</sup> 22, Mn<sup>3+</sup> 22, Co<sup>3+</sup> 24, Fe<sup>3+</sup> 23. Only Cr<sup>2+</sup> and Mn<sup>3+</sup> match, so n = 2.
Two moles of AgCl means two ionisable chlorides: complex = [Co(en)<sub>2</sub>(NH<sub>3</sub>)Cl]Cl<sub>2</sub>.
Co is +3 (d<sup>6</sup>) with strong-field en/NH<sub>3</sub> ligands, low spin: t<sub>2g</sub><sup>6</sup>e<sub>g</sub><sup>0</sup>. Electrons in t<sub>2g</sub> = 6.

qs.stem:
For strong electrolyte Λm increases slowly with dilution and can be represented by the equation
Λm = Λm° − A c1/2
Molar conductivity values of the solutions of strong electrolyte AB at 18°C are given below:
c (mol L−1): 0.04, 0.09, 0.16, 0.25
Λm (S cm2 mol−1): 96.1, 95.7, 95.3, 94.9
The value of constant A based on the above data [in S cm2 mol−1/(mol/L)1/2] unit is ____ .
steps: Use √c: 0.04 gives 0.2 and 0.09 gives 0.3, so the slope is A = −ΔΛ/Δ√c.
Check: Λ° = 96.1 + 4(0.2) = 96.9; at c = 0.25, 96.9 − 4(0.5) = 94.9, which matches.

qs.stem:
A → B (First Reaction)
C → D (Second Reaction)
Consider the above two first-order reactions. The rate constant for first reaction at 500 K is double of the same at 300 K. At 500 K, 50% of the reaction becomes complete in 2 hour. The activation energy of the second reaction is half of that of first reaction. If the rate constant at 500 K of the second reaction becomes double of the rate constant of the first reaction at the same temperature; then rate constant for the second reaction at 300 K is __________ ×10−1 hour−1 (nearest integer).
steps: First reaction at 500 K: t<sub>1/2</sub> = 2 h, so k<sub>1</sub> = ln 2/2. Second reaction at 500 K: k<sub>2</sub> = 2k<sub>1</sub> = ln 2 h<sup>−1</sup>.
For the first reaction, ln 2 = (E<sub>a1</sub>/R)(1/300 − 1/500), so (E<sub>a1</sub>/R)(1/300 − 1/500) = ln 2.
E<sub>a2</sub> = E<sub>a1</sub>/2, so ln(k<sub>2,500</sub>/k<sub>2,300</sub>) = (ln 2)/2, i.e. k<sub>2,500</sub>/k<sub>2,300</sub> = √2.
k<sub>2,300</sub> = ln 2/√2 = 0.49 h<sup>−1</sup> = 4.9 × 10<sup>−1</sup> ≈ 5 × 10<sup>−1</sup>.

qs.stem: Two positively charged particles m<sub>1</sub> and m<sub>2</sub> have been accelerated across the same potential difference of 200 keV in vacuum. [Given mass of m<sub>1</sub> = 1 amu and m<sub>2</sub> = 4 amu] The de Broglie wavelength of m<sub>1</sub> will be x times of m<sub>2</sub>. The value of x is ______ (nearest integer)
steps: Both gain the same kinetic energy (same charge and potential difference assumed), so p = √(2mK) and λ = h/√(2mK) ∝ 1/√m.
λ<sub>1</sub>/λ<sub>2</sub> = √(m<sub>2</sub>/m<sub>1</sub>) = √4 = 2.
